THESE APPEALS ARE COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
These two appeals are filed challenging the judgment and award dated 14.10.2019 passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge MACT, Srirangapatna in M.V.C.No.1021/2017.

entities.text: Additional Senior Civil Judge MACT, Srirangapatna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appeal preferred by the claimants is on the ground of inadequate compensation and seeking for enhancement of the compensation.

Whereas, the appeal preferred by the Insurance Company i.e., National Insurance Company Ltd, which was respondent No.4 before the tribunal is to set aside the judgment and award, fixing the liability of 25% against the said insurer - Car, which was involved in the accident.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
NC: 2024:KHC:14598 That on 08.07.2017 at about 5.50 p.m, one Ms. Manjula.P was travelling along with her colleague Thanujkumar on a Bullet bike bearing registration No.KA-02-JK-2151 as a pillion rider, as they were going on excursion/picnic along with other Motorbike riders and pillion riders in a group.
During which time the driver of the bike rode the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner in a high speed and dashed against the road divider.
Due to which pillion rider Ms.Manjula was thrown out from the bike and fell down on the other side of the road by crossing the divider.
Meanwhile, the driver of Ertiga Car bearing registration No.KA-42-M-5335 came from the other direction and ran over the said Manjula.
Due to which she sustained severe head injuries and injuries on other parts of the body.
Unfortunately she succumbed to the injuries on the way to the Hospital on the same day.

The claimants are none other than the unfortunate parents of deceased Manjula, filed claim petition seeking compensation against the respondent i.e., the owner of the Bullet Motorbike and the owner of the Ertiga Car, along with their respective insurers.
3. On service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 3 i.e., owner of the Bullet bike and owner of the Ertiga Car were NC: 2024:KHC:14598 placed ex-parte.
Respondent Nos.2 and 4 filed the statement of objections.

It was a plea taken by respondent Nos.2 and 4 denying the claim of the claimant,
including age, avocation, income and so also the negligence attributed against the respective insured vehicle and also the compensation claim to be exorbitant.

Respondent No.2, the insurer of the Motorbike pleaded that the rider of the bike did not possess a valid and effective Driving License as on the date of occurrence of the accident and sought for observing the liability against the Insurance Company, so also, respondent No.4 pleaded that there was absolutely no negligence on the part of the driver of the Car.
The entire negligence was on the part of the rider of the Motorbike against whom Charge sheet was filed.
Based on this, sought for absolving any liability against respondent No.4.
Accordingly, these two Insurance Companies sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

sentences.text: On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

3.2. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined herself as PW.1 and another as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents as NC: 2024:KHC:14598 Exs.P1 to P30.

On the other hand, respondents got examined as RW.1 and RW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.R1 to R3.
3.3.

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.31,70,000/- and fastened the liability jointly and severally against respondent Nos.2 and 4, the Insurance companies of respondent Nos.1 and 3 to an extent of 75% and 25% against the respondent Nos.2 and 4 respectively and directed to pay the compensation within 30 days from the date of the award along with interest at 9% per annum.
3.4. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, the claimants are before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

Whereas, one of the Insurance Company i.e., Insurer of the Car is before this Court seeking to set aside fastening of 25% contributory negligence and to set aside the judgment and award as against the said Insurance Company.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the claimants and learned counsel for both the Insurance Companies i.e., insurer NC: 2024:KHC:14598 of the Motorbike and insurer of the Car.
On careful perusal of the records, it is seen that initially FIR was filed against both the vehicles.

Thereafter,
Charge sheet has been laid against the rider of the Motorbike.
Therefore, negligence has been rightly proved and established as against the rider of the Motorbike and involvement of the Car to a certain extent.

5. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for the claimants that tribunal has awarded meagre compensation without taking into consideration the gross income and therefore, the compensation requires to be enhanced by taking higher income, so also, on other heads.
The compensation calls for marginal enhancement.

6. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company, who is in appeal i.e., the insurer of the Ertiga Car,
vehemently contends that the tribunal has committed a gross error in fastening liability of 25%
contributory negligence.
Whereas, the entire negligence was against the rider of the Motorbike, who rode the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the divider.
Due to this the pillion rider was thrown out onto the opposite side of the road across the divider and fell on the extreme left side of the road.
Due to which the NC: 2024:KHC:14598 Ertiga Car which was coming from east to west ran over the deceased Manjula.

Therefore, the question of fastening contributory negligence against the Ertiga Car is erroneous for the reason that the accident occurred due to the rashness and negligence of the rider of the Motorbike.
There is no rashness or negligence against the driver of the Car.

The Charge sheet is filed only against the rider of the Motorbike, when such an accident takes place and there is a split second for contemplating and anticipating the situation, the question of maneuvering the Car or avoiding the accident, is very remotely impossible.

Hence, he contends that the entire negligence has to be attributed against the rider of the Motorbike for the Smt Sumangala vs Thanujakumar M V on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102276932/
5 rashness, negligence in riding the Motorbike.

Learned counsels representing the Insurance Company of the Bullet Motorbike,
Sri.A.N.Krishnaswamy and Sri.D. Vijaya Kumar vehemently contend that the judgment and award passed by the tribunal is correct, same does not call for interference.

sentences.text: It is a well reasoned judgment taking into consideration all the possibilities including the police records, the spot sketch and the evidence adduced by the claimants as well as the witnesses.

With regard to contributory negligence,
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:14598 learned counsel appearing on behalf of the insurer of the Motorbike sustained the contributory negligence of 25% fastened against the owner of the Ertiga Car contends that the deceased was thrown onto the other side of the road, but if there had been little care and caution taken by the driver of the Ertiga Car, may be the further damage and the magnitude of the injuries leading to the death could have been avoided.
Either he had been very fast in driving or if he was slow, certainly he could have avoided the accident.

8. While dealing with the Motor accident claims cases of road traffic accident, this Court need not rely exclusively on the police records for the purpose of awarding compensation, no doubt it is an added evidentiary and material value to be taken for determining the compensation and negligence.
However, the tribunal or this Court dealing with the road traffic accident, is not required to see "proof beyond reasonable doubt".

What is required to be seen is the "preponderance of probability"
and the involvement of the vehicle.

In the present case, it is not the case of the insurer of the Car that the vehicle was not at all involved in the occurrence of the accident which ran over the deceased Manjula after she was thrown from the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:14598 Motorbike to the other side of the road.

Under the circumstances, considering all these aspects the tribunal has passed very well reasoned order by fastening marginal contributory negligence of 25% against the Car and the major contributory negligence of 75% against the rider of the Motorbike, which in my opinion is justifiable, does not call for interference.

9. Now coming to the aspect of enhancement of compensation which is argued by the learned counsel for the claimants, the tribunal has taken the income of six months on an average and calculated Rs.20,000/- p.m as the income for awarding compensation and the appropriate multiplier has been taken '17' for age of 28 years.
Calculated 50% towards future prospects, as the deceased was working in a private company earning a regular constant income, same does not call for interference.

Though learned counsel for the appellant- Insurance Company has pleaded that the future prospects ought to have been awarded at 40% rather than 50% but this Court is not inclined to accept such an argument, 50% awarded by the tribunal is retained.

The deduction of 50% is also correct as the deceased was spinster and unmarried, hence,

sentences.text: Under the circumstances, I do not find any reason to add any value to the argument put forth by the learned counsel for the claimants for enhancement of compensation as it is just and reasonable.

10. With regard to the argument put forth by learned counsel for the Insurance Company-appellant as well as the respondent on the ground that the interest awarded by the tribunal is on the higher side.

I am inclined to accept such an argument that the interest awarded at 9% is on the higher side,
same requires to be reduced to 6% per annum.
11.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company of the Motorbike vehemently contends that once the interest rate is reduced because of the appeal preferred by one of the Insurance Companies, the same should hold parity with the other Insurance Company which in good faith and generosity has deposited interest at 9% p.a.

I am inclined to accept the - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:14598 argument which is very attractive and also holds water for the reason that there as to be parity of awarding interest and though the other Insurance Company is not in appeal,
and one of the Insurance Companies is in appeal on the ground of interest, which is reduced to 6%,
the other Insurance Company cannot be fastened with interest at the rate of 9%.
Hence, the interest component for the Insurance Companies i.e., respondent Nos.2 and 4 together is reduced to 6% p.a from the date of petition.
